name: All Good
description: Thumbs up with OK hand to double-confirm everything is good or approved.
meaning: Used to show strong approval or confirmation. Everything is not just okay, it's double-confirmed good. The thumbs-up says 'I like this' and the OK hand says 'and I confirm it,' which makes the combo the standard send for a clean sign-off or a quick green-light in a work chat or a group thread.
seoDescription: What does 👍👌 mean? The thumbs up and OK hand combo explained. Used for strong approval and confirmation.

longForm.overview:
👍👌 stacks the thumbs-up on top of the OK hand, and the move from 'this is good' to 'this is fully confirmed good' is the whole point. 👍 alone reads as light approval; 👌 alone reads as a casual checkmark. Put them together and the combo says the sender is signing off on the moment twice over — they like it, they confirm it, and they do not need to elaborate. The combination lands as the standard 'we are locked in' beat on Slack, iMessage, and in group chats where someone just wants to register agreement without typing out a sentence.

On work chat threads and in tight friend groups 👍👌 is the default reaction to a quick confirmation, a green-light, or a settled plan. The combo is friendly, neutral, and unambiguously positive, so it works in nearly any setting where the sender wants to land as agreeable. The redundancy is what gives the combo its strength: a single 👍 reads as casual; a single 👌 reads as a tiny OK; the combo reads as 'I am with you, full stop.'

👍👌 also doubles as a closing beat in a quick exchange — sending 👍👌 instead of 'cool, thanks' tells the other person the thread is done and they can move on. The OK hand in slot two softens the thumbs-up's slightly corporate energy, which keeps the combo from drifting into robotic territory. Writers should use it when the agreement is genuine and complete; for a softer 'I see this' beat, a single 👍 is plenty.
longForm.howPeopleUseIt:
👍👌 usually arrives as a quick reply to confirm a meeting time, an order number, a deadline, or a small piece of news that needed an acknowledgment. It is the go-to beat in work chat threads when a manager confirms a date, a coworker closes a loop, or a client signs off on a deliverable. The combo also lands as a friendly green-light from a friend when plans are locked in.

The combo works as a closing message in a thread that has run its course. Sending 👍👌 instead of 'got it, thanks' tells the other person the exchange is over and they can stop typing. In family group chats 👍👌 shows up as a 'yes, I will be there' to a holiday plan, a 'cool, see you then' to a kid's pickup, or a 'sounds good' to a logistics note. The redundancy of the gesture plus the symbol is what makes the combo feel final.
longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 👍👌 when the recipient needs a real response rather than a quick sign-off — sending 👍👌 to a friend who just shared a problem reads as a brush-off. Avoid it when the conversation is still unfolding and the other person is waiting on detail; the combo lands as 'I am closing this' even when the sender did not mean it that way.

Also avoid 👍👌 in customer-support threads where the issue is unresolved; the combo can read as cold or sarcastic when the recipient is still waiting on a fix. And avoid the 👌 symbol entirely in regions or platforms where the OK hand has been read as a hate signal in the last few years — the round-the-thumb gesture has a charged history, and a single 👍 is the safer choice if you are unsure of your audience.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends you 👍👌 and you want to keep the bit going, mirror with another 👍👌 or a 'sounds good' to register the same agreement. If you want to slow the conversation down, a single 👍 or a 'got it' also lands as acknowledgment without the finality.

If the 👍👌 landed on a question that actually needs a sentence, follow up with a real reply and the conversation will pick up where it left off. If a friend is using the combo as a closing beat and you want to keep chatting, send a softer reaction like 😊 or a follow-up question so the thread stays alive.

faqs.question: What does 👍👌 mean?
faqs.answer: 👍👌 means the sender is locking in agreement twice over. The thumbs-up says 'this is good' and the OK hand says 'and I confirm it.'

faqs.question: Is 👍👌 passive aggressive?
faqs.answer: 👍👌 can read as passive aggressive when it lands on a long message that deserved a real reply. In quick work threads it reads as a clean sign-off.

faqs.question: What does 👍👌 mean from a guy?
faqs.answer: From a guy or anyone else, 👍👌 means the sender agrees with what was just said. There is no gendered meaning; the combo is about the strength of the agreement, not who is sending it.

faqs.question: What does 👍👌 mean on Slack?
faqs.answer: On Slack 👍👌 usually closes a thread about a confirmed meeting, a green-lit decision, or a settled plan. Coworkers read it as 'we are good, moving on.'

conversationExamples.interpretation: Work thread confirmation. Mirror with 👍👌 or a 'got it, see you then' to close the loop.
Friend group plans locked. Mirror with 👍👌 or a 'see you there' to register agreement.
Family logistics closeout. Mirror with 👍👌 or a 'thanks, see you then' to confirm.
Date confirmation. Mirror with 👍👌 or a 'looking forward to it' to keep the warmth.
Group chat win. Mirror with 🙌 or a thank-you sentence to share the celebration.
